notes: Building and Industrial News, vol. 12 part 2 (Internet Archive buildingindustri12212cont), the 27 weekly issues from 2 July to 31 December 1912, all Tuesdays. Same method as the later volumes of this source and the Building and Engineering News run that follows it: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll year fits, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before the work. The issues were dated from their covers ('Issued Weekly ... Twelfth Year, No. 27' to 'No. 53'); the issue of 16 July runs to 76 leaves because it carries the plates of the City Hall competition. extract.py ran with BEN_LOOSE=1; item numbers the OCR misread were corrected from the page image. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; a cost or name not legible on the image, or past a column or page break, was left out, and where the printed total and the printed instalments disagree no cost is given (Union and Leavenworth). Nine entries cut by a column break were finished from the OCR text of the next column, and a cost was taken from it only where the instalments add up to the total. Owners who are private individuals are never recorded, nor is a contractor or architect who is the owner, shares the owner's surname, or is listed at the owner's premises; sureties are cut. Held back at the image (75 of 228): minor work such as signs, ovens, small repairs and partitions (28), contracts the page already carries in full from the San Francisco Call (21), storey, unit or use counts that contradict the roll (15), and small alterations and plain single houses on parcels with no page (11, held for a page). 43 of the picked rows were on pages that already carry a Call entry of the same fortnight (the 1906-1913 newspaper recovery): 19 were dropped as above (the other two drops repeat a row of this volume) and 20 were trimmed to what this paper adds (the architect, the contractor or the price); the rest are different contracts for the same building. Where the price differs from the Call entry the page image read here is given and the Call entry left alone (864 Francisco Street: $9,385 here, $8,386 in the Call entry; 2259 Green Street: $4,050 here, $4,030 there). The permit of 3 September for one-storey and mezzanine brick stores at Polk and Green (Bothin Real Estate Co.) is published as a record only; the building on the page is the four-storey one permitted in April 1913. The permit of 3 December for a foundation at Lake Street and Twentieth Avenue does not set the architect of the building the page describes. One held fact of the later run (731 Washington Street, 29 October 1919) was read against its page image and taken up when this volume seeded the page; the held contract for 1274-76 Eighth Avenue (28 May 1919) reads $450 on the image, not $15,500, and stays held as minor work.

coverage.remaining: Unread: the two 1911 half-year volumes on the Internet Archive (vol. 11 pt. 1 and pt. 2). In this volume: 131 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; they still need the image check), and 11 more were held for a page at the image. 827 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today. The rest have a nearest parcel that was not accepted.
